clue.text: Mother's meeting son for church service

parts.note: mother is MA, and the possessive adds an S

explanation.surface: A mother joins her son to go to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mother's' gives MA plus the possessive S, then 'meeting' joins the S for son.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catholic Eucharist service is called by this name.

clue.text: Story a nobleman read aloud

indicators.note: something read aloud is heard rather than seen, so we want a word that sounds like the phrase

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman, so the phrase gives A COUNT

explanation.surface: Someone recites a tale about an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative or report of events is a synonym for a story.

clue.text: Stain ruined shiny material

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters of the word before are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A mark has spoiled a glossy fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: This smooth glossy weave is a classic shiny fabric.

clue.text: Fool takes the plunge a short time later

indicators.note: later says the short time comes after the plunge in the answer

parts.note: to take a plunge into water is to dip, here DIPS
a tick is a moment, as in 'just a tick'

explanation.surface: A silly person dives in and soon regrets it.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a dipstick is an idiot, a mild insult.

clue.text: Mark time after celebration

indicators.note: after places the time letter behind the celebration word

parts.note: a do is a British informal word for a party

explanation.surface: Someone notes the hour once the party is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A small spot or point is a kind of mark.

clue.text: Ate out, having photograph taken

parts.note: pic is short for picture or photograph
nicked is British slang for stolen, taken

explanation.surface: Someone dined outdoors and had a photo snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Eating a meal outdoors on a rug is exactly what this verb describes.

clue.text: Satellite rattles around

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of the word before are moved about into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An orbiting object makes a rattling noise as it goes around.
explanation.walkthrough: Telstar was the famous 1962 communications satellite.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the name of an early communications satellite launched in 1962.

clue.text: Business we run will make you cringe

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: The company we manage will embarrass you.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink back in fear is a synonym for cringe.

clue.text: Very happy not moving east of the city

indicators.note: in an across answer, east of means placed to the right of the city letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London
static means stationary, not moving

explanation.surface: Someone is delighted to stay put just outside town.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, whose postcodes begin EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overjoyed or thrilled is a synonym for very happy.

clue.text: Grass in Cornwall bending backwards

indicators.note: bending backwards says the letters found are then read from right to left
in says the letters sit inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Grass in a Cornish field leans over in the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of mown grass in a garden is what this word names.

clue.text: Feel very hot running water?

definitions.meaning: to feel scorching or on fire, as a face does with embarrassment
a Scottish word for a stream or brook, water that runs

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if heat can be cooled by a running tap.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to be scorching; the other is the Scots word for a small stream.

clue.text: Swellings on skin? Surgeon's put on first of bandages

indicators.note: put on says the surgeon's name is placed after the bandage letter
first of means only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: Joseph Lister was the pioneering surgeon of antiseptics; his name plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: A surgeon dresses skin swellings, starting with bandages.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Lister was the Victorian surgeon who pioneered antiseptic surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluid-filled bumps on the skin from friction or burns are these swellings.

clue.text: Agent's business bankrupt? Anger ensues

indicators.note: ensues means follows, so the anger word comes after the bankrupt word

parts.note: broke means penniless, bankrupt
rage is fury, strong anger

explanation.surface: An agency goes bust and fury follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A broker is an agent, and the trade a broker runs takes this name.

clue.text: Workshop producing piece of jewellery I love

parts.note: a stud is a small earring or ornament
love is zero in tennis, shown as O

explanation.surface: An artisan's workshop turns out jewellery that the speaker adores.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's or craftsman's workroom is a synonym for a workshop.

clue.text: Protection from French swordsman if cut

parts.note: de is French for from

indicators.note: cut says the swordsman word loses its tail letter

parts.note: a fencer is someone who fights with a sword in sport

explanation.surface: A French swordsman protects himself if wounded.
explanation.definitionFit: Guarding against attack is the meaning of this word, a synonym of protection.

clue.text: Sailors boarding part of ship? That's it in a nutshell

indicators.note: boarding means getting on board, so the sailors go inside the ship part

parts.note: the keel is the backbone along the bottom of a ship
RN is the Royal Navy, sailors

explanation.surface: Sailors climbing aboard sums up the whole matter.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works two ways: the essence of a matter, and literally the seed inside a nut's shell.
explanation.definitionFit: The core or essence of something, and literally the edible seed found inside a nut's shell.

clue.text: Intercity train, say

definitions.meaning: a fast train making few stops between cities
to put into words, to state

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a fast train; the other means to voice or state something.

clue.text: US president glared, if put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters of the words before are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An American leader scowled when annoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: James Garfield was the 20th US president, assassinated in 1881.
explanation.definitionFit: James A. Garfield served as the twentieth American head of state.

clue.text: Fruit drink is about a couple of pence

indicators.note: is about means surrounds, so the drink goes round the pence

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink
P is a penny, so two of them make PP

explanation.surface: A fruit drink costs about two pence.
explanation.definitionFit: A common orchard fruit, round and crisp, is what this word names.

clue.text: One employed in women's gym to clean

indicators.note: employed in means working inside, so the numeral goes within the other letters

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
PE is physical education, school gym
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A cleaner is hired at a ladies' gym.
explanation.definitionFit: To rub a surface free of dirt with a cloth is to clean it.

clue.text: We don't say a word about large British people

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
SH is the hushing sound asking for silence

explanation.surface: We keep quiet about the big people of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The people of Wales are a British nation.

clue.text: Communicative old writer

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: An elderly author is chatty.
explanation.definitionFit: Being frank and forthcoming, sharing thoughts freely, is a synonym for communicative.

clue.text: Greek war hero unwell, beset by pains

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the pains go round the sickness word

parts.note: aches are pains
ill means sick, unwell

explanation.surface: A Greek warrior falls sick, suffering pains.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the great warrior of the Trojan War in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Headgear not initially expected in hot weather

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is dropped from the hot weather word

parts.note: heat is hot weather, as in a heatwave

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A sunhat is unexpectedly needed in a heatwave.
explanation.definitionFit: A covering worn on the head is the plainest kind of headgear.

clue.text: Rented accommodation: temporary shelter housing European people

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the shelter goes round the other letters

parts.note: a tent is a portable, temporary shelter
men are people

explanation.surface: A shelter put up to house European workers is let out.
explanation.definitionFit: A large building divided into rented flats, typically crowded, is this kind of dwelling.

clue.text: Enjoys hot cooked meat dish

parts.note: to have is to enjoy, as in having a good time; here HAS
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone relishes a hot plate of cooked meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of chopped cooked meat fried with potatoes goes by this name.
